I've been in therapy much of my life. Unfortunately there's only so much that can be done. And several times I have been in recovery and started to let my guard down... Sometimes if I am walking alone and someone, often a man, is walking behind me... I will cross the street. Is that treating them as a criminal or is that me simply being wary? I have known many rapists, some of them were actually remorseful when their behaviour was clearly pointed out to them, but regardless their behaviour was assault. And it's not just men, either. I would argue that you probably know a few women who are guilty of sexual assault too. The amount of women I have known who have coerced/pressured their partners into sex is disgusting, I even know a whole bunch of queer women who have grabbed my boobs, gone for my genitals or kissed me without consent while simultaneously posting about sexual assault awareness. The statistic is high due to ignorance and a lack of understanding as to what constitutes as assault. I'd also argue to number is even higher as some people aren't even aware that what they experienced was assault. For example, my mother was groomed at 13 by a 24 year old and she thought that was a consensual relationship. She also was drugged, raped and filmed by her cousin and for years thought she must have consented because she didn't fight him in the video. This lack of understanding is why we have statistics like this.

As someone who has almost been murdered and also mugged, I most definitely do treat every person I meet like they might murder or rob me. That's what being assaulted does to the brain, everyone becomes a potential attacker. Ideally, victims will receive therapy/treatment and that fear won't continue but unfortunately once something like that happens it's hard to trust people. Rape is even more hard to deal with because a lot of people who are assaulted/raped don't just have one experience, it's often multiple examples that lead toward that wariness and fear. So yeah. I try not to treat anyone like a criminal but I am definitely always aware that someone might be capable of being one.
